newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire president Mobutu may leave hospital Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire president Mobutu may leave hospital Tuesday.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, receiving more cancer treatment in Monaco as rebels advance in his country, may leave hospital on Tuesday morning, a presidential spokesman said on Monday.
The spokesman denied press reports that Mobutu, 66, was in a serious condition.

The Zairean leader was admitted to Princess Grace hospital in Monte Carlo on Sunday for further treatment related to his prostate cancer, a day after Tutsi rebels led by Laurent Kabila captured Zaire's third-largest city, Kisangani, almost without a fight.

"He went into hospital Sunday afternoon for additional treatment and could come out tomorrow morning," spokesman Gad Cohen told Reuters. Cohen said he "totally denied" all reports that Mobutu's health had seriously deteriorated.
This was the first time the president's aides had talked of "treatment" at the Monaco hospital. They described his previous visits there as being for routine tests.
The ragged Zairean army has lost a fifth of the country's territory to the rebels since they launched their offensive last October, with troops looting and retreating.
Kabila has refused United Nations calls for a ceasefire and vowed to go all the way to Kinshasa to oust Mobutu and "liberate" Zaire.

The president, one of Africa's longest-serving strongmen, has spent most of the last eight months at his French Riviera villa at Roquebrune-Cap Martin since undergoing prostate surgery in Switzerland last August.
He was given a triumphant welcome when he returned to Kinshasa in December by crowds who believed he could save the country from collapse.

But after announcing a counter-offensive, hiring foreign mercenaries and shaking up the army, he refused to negotiate with the rebels or compromise with his political opponents and withdrew to his jungle palace in Gbadolite, about 1,000 km (600 miles) from the capital.
Mobutu returned to France on February 21 and had been planning to go back to Zaire last week, according to his son and spokesman Mobutu Nzanga, but his departure was delayed.
Before he was taken to hospital on Sunday, an official in his entourage had said Mobutu might return to his country later this week but there were no final plans for him to do so.
